sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Merged main (9.99.970) into perf-steps-1-4, then fixed a bug the merge's own conflict resolution introduced: runFilter()'s single-table branch had one real conflict, where main's block re-invoked several cloneNode-era re-wiring calls (initExpandRGsFeature/_cdtocInitTracklistToggles/_rewireNestedTableH2Toggles/initAnnotationCompareRadios/initPicardTaggerColumn(rewireOnly)/a full initCaaPics()/initEaaPics() re-run) that PERFORMANCE.org Step 1's in-place filtering (5d7f835) already made redundant on this branch — correctly dropped. But that same main block also contained _artHighlightAllBuiltCaaCells() (added by main's fbb5355, the query-dependent CAA per-image type/comment highlight sweep for content whose ul.mb-caa-art-ul was baked in as static HTML rather than built through _artEnrichIcon() — e.g. disk-loaded pages), which is NOT covered by Step 1's reasoning since it re-applies highlighting for the CURRENT filter query, not a one-time init. Dropping it wholesale left the function defined but never called, reproducing exactly the '0 highlight spans' symptom fbb5355 had fixed on main. Restored the call (in runFilter()'s in-place-filter block, alongside the existing CAA/EAA bigbox sync) with a comment distinguishing it from the genuinely-redundant calls. Verified the disk-load pipeline's own single-table CAA/EAA init block (~line 56831) already independently covers initCaaPics()/initEaaPics()/the completion-toast registration, so nothing else from main's dropped block was missing. tests/live/registry.org's artist-releases-filter-sort.spec.js note also updated — it still described the CAA highlighting as an unfixed 'confirmed-live UNSTABLE quirk' using skipHighlightCheck, which was accurate before main's fbb5355 but stale after it (that commit replaced skipHighlightCheck with exact expectHighlightCount/highlightTextSet assertions on all 4 CAA FILTER_CASES); fbb5355 never touched registry.org so the note never caught up.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: PERFORMANCE.org Step 14: added in-flight request de-duplication to the shared CAA/EAA image cache (_artFetchCachedImage) — a concurrent request for the identical front-thumbnail URL now joins the already-running IDB read/network fetch instead of issuing a duplicate one, via a new _artInFlightFetches Map. Closes a race where a row's inline CAA/EAA thumbnail (Release column), the separate CAA/EAA column's own "main" icon, and the release-group bigbox strip — all three of which already fetch the byte-identical front-thumbnail URL through the same three-tier cache — could each miss the cache and independently hit the network. Tier 2/3 (IndexedDB lookup + network fallback) was split out into a new _artFetchUncachedImage() helper so the de-dup bookkeeping wraps a single call; no change to any call site (_artLoadIcon, the inline loadTask, _loadBigImgIdb, _caaFetchStats). Applies uniformly to CAA and EAA, inline/column/bigbox pipelines. The separate count/type (back cover, medium, spine, booklet, …) enrichment fetch is unaffected — it hits a structurally different JSON endpoint and cannot be served by this reuse. Also added window.__saTest.fetchCachedImageConcurrent(url, n) (test-mode debug hook, no production behavior change) so tests/live/caa-icon-fetch-dedup.spec.js can exercise the de-dup deterministically — reproducing the concurrent-overlap window through the live render pipeline turned out not to be reliable from outside; the shared queue's own FIFO scheduling serializes same-URL requests across pipelines closely enough that no genuine overlap occurred on the pilot test page.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: PERFORMANCE.org: added a consolidated "Session summary" section with all measured comparison data from the 2026-08-24 artist-events investigation (main vs perf-steps-1-4 vs perf-steps-3-4) — narrow-filter headline table, the wide-filter finding that flips the winner (main scales linearly with match count, perf-steps-1-4 is roughly constant), the traced forced-reflow root cause with a per-sub-step breakdown table, the content-visibility/table-layout:fixed mitigation attempt (negative result, not implemented), the sort-skip fix's internal-vs-external measurement gap and its methodology lesson, the Step 5 CAA/EAA queue-completion comparison (main never completes within 180s, perf-steps-1-4 completes in 42.2s), the perf-steps-3-4 cross-check confirming Steps 3-4 have zero regression on their own, and an overall takeaways/recommendation subsection. No ShowAllEntityData.user.js changes.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: PERFORMANCE.org Steps 1-2 follow-up: single-table sort no longer calls `runFilter()` after reordering the live DOM when no global/column filter is currently active — with nothing to hide and no highlight spans to reapply, that call was pure no-op work (the full-table forced-layout cost Steps 1-2 already pay once per action, paid a second time for nothing). New shared `_hasAnyActiveSingleTableFilter()` helper (next to `stripFilterPrefix`/`stripColFilterPrefix`) gates the skip; multi-table mode is unaffected (always calls `runFilter()` as before). Measured on `artist-events` (4174 rows): self-reported internal JS duration dropped ~995ms from ~2842ms, but — important caveat found while measuring — external/user-perceived wall-clock time only dropped a more modest ~15-20% (not the ~65% the internal number alone suggested), because removing the forced synchronous reflow doesn't eliminate that layout cost, it defers it to whenever the browser or a later DOM read next needs it. Verified via `tests/live/artist-events-interactions.spec.js` (all 5 tests still pass) and a full `post-filter.html`/`post-sort.html` diff against the previous baseline: the only difference anywhere in either capture is two inline `style="color:..."` attributes (`#mb-sort-status-display`'s color correctly flipping green now that its self-reported duration crossed the same color threshold lower; `#mb-filter-status-display`'s color differs by ordinary timing noise in an unrelated, untouched code path) — no row content, count, or order changed.

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: tests: added artist-events performance-comparison instrumentation — `tests/live/artist-events-interactions.spec.js` (global/column filter, sort both directions, header-badge sanity, uniq-dropdown cache-invalidation correctness), `tests/support/capture-interaction-perf.js` (median-of-5 timing for global filter/column filter/sort/uniq-dropdown cold-vs-warm-open, written per-branch to `tests/snapshots/artist-events/interaction-perf-<branch>.json` so `main` and this branch can be compared side by side), and `tests/support/capture-snapshots.js` extended with `post-filter.html`/`post-sort.html` full-DOM regression snapshots for `artist-events` (catching a rendering regression WIP.1-WIP.7's in-place-mutation rewrite could introduce that no single correctness assertion would catch). All three load via the newly-captured `tests/fixtures/saved-data/artist-events.json.gz` disk fixture (`tests/support/capture-fixture.js`, extended with an `artist-events` entry and `seedGmValues`/`renderTimeout` support) rather than a live 42-page fetch. Canonical filter/sort/uniq-drop targets shared across all three via new `tests/support/artistEventsFixture.js`, so they can't drift apart. New `waitForActualRowCount()` helper in `tests/support/filterSortAssertions.js` — a stronger completion signal than the existing status-text-based waits for an action that narrows a large single-table page then widens it back out (confirmed empirically that `#mb-filter-status-display`/`.mb-row-count-stat` both update before the tbody rebuild and the `#mb-render-heading` chunked-render overlay have actually finished catching up, on `artist-events`' 4174 rows). No `ShowAllEntityData.user.js` changes — pure test-infra additions, authored on `main` and merged in here, per this project's existing precedent for test-only commits.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: PERFORMANCE.org Step 5 follow-up: fixed a visible stall on large lazy-loaded tables (sa_caa_io_threshold, e.g. an 800-row series/events page) where dragging the scrollbar quickly to a distant part of the table showed only the header row for a moment before rows appeared — a scroll-jank/checkerboard symptom, not missing row data (all rows are fully built at initial render, unchanged since before Step 5). Root cause: a fast scrollbar-drag jump brings dozens/hundreds of off-screen icons within the IntersectionObserver's 200px root margin at once, and the callback previously ran that whole batch's unobserve+enqueue work synchronously in a single task, competing with the browser for the main thread it needed to paint the just-scrolled-to rows — a collision that couldn't happen before Step 5, since all artwork loaded once at initial render, before the user had started scrolling. Fixed with a new _artProcessIoEntriesBatched(), which splits the callback's intersecting entries into 20-entry chunks (_ART_IO_BATCH_SIZE) and processes one chunk per requestAnimationFrame instead of the whole burst in one tick; _artInitLazyPics()'s observer callback now delegates to it. Does not change any request-concurrency queue — only spreads the DOM-mutation cost of starting observer-triggered loads/enrichment across frames.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: PERFORMANCE.org Step 5 (lazy CAA/EAA loading via IntersectionObserver): for tables at or above a new sa_caa_io_threshold setting (default 500 data rows), CAA/EAA icon background-image loads and JSON-API enrichment are deferred until each artwork-icon cell scrolls within 200px of the viewport, instead of firing for every row at initial render. A persistent per-archive IntersectionObserver (_caaArtIO / _eaaArtIO) is created once by the new _artInitLazyPics() and observes every icon in the table; on intersect it unobserves the element and enqueues the same _artLoadIcon()/_artEnrichIcon() calls the eager path already used, through the shared _caaQueue. The observer survives filter/sort passes since Step 1 keeps allRows as live DOM rows and initCaaPics()/initEaaPics() now run once per render instead of per keystroke; _artInitQueue() (the shared once-per-render-pass reset point already used for _caaQueue) now also disconnects and nulls any previous _caaArtIO/_eaaArtIO so a fresh render observes the current DOM set. Below the threshold, when IntersectionObserver is unavailable, or when the setting is 0, both paths run eagerly exactly as before. Reimplemented from archive/filter-performance-fix-v1-single-table's WIP.2 ("Pattern 5") against current main; the big-picture strip above the table (_artInitBigPics) is unaffected — only the per-row icon column and its enrichment are deferred, matching the archived branch's scope.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: PERFORMANCE.org Step 4 (openUniqDrop() per-open caching): the unique-values dropdown's 5 full tbody.rows scan passes (whole-cell value counts, flag-icon segment map, relationship-cell detection, relationship icon counts, inline CAA/EAA-thumbnail counts) now share Step 3's exact caching primitive — a per-(table, column) WeakMap cache keyed by a signature of the currently visible rows' data-mb-row-idx values, via the shared _visibleRowSetSignature() added in Step 3. Reopening the same column's dropdown with no filter/sort change in between skips straight past all 5 passes. Found and fixed one correctness gap while implementing: the "Cell structure" section's collapsed/expanded split is read from expandedCells (individually-toggled cells), not derivable from the visible-row signature, so a lone cell expand/collapse click would otherwise leave a reopened dropdown showing a stale split. Added _invalidateUniqDropDataCache(table, colIndex) and wired it into all 5 places expandedCells is mutated by user interaction (_applyCollapseState()'s two branches, ensureCollapseDelegate()'s three inline toggle branches). Also gated the roleTokenValueCounts Map (an 'Entity info - Role' feature main grew independently since the original branch work) behind the same cache and added it to the stored bundle, so it doesn't come back empty on a cache hit.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: PERFORMANCE.org Step 3 (cache _updateAllColHeaderCounts): the per-column unique-value/multi-row header-count scan (O(rows x columns), the file's own documented worst case) now memoizes its result per <table> against a cheap O(rows) signature of the currently visible rows' data-mb-row-idx values, and skips the full recompute whenever that signature is unchanged since the last call. This makes syncCollapseButtonsWithColumnVisibility's column show/hide re-init and multi-table sub-table re-renders free when the visible row set hasn't actually changed. The one known call site that mutates cell CONTENT in place without changing which rows are visible — initReleaseEventsColumn()'s two post-population re-scans of initCollapsableColumns(), which fill previously-empty Release events/country/date cells — now explicitly calls the new _invalidateColHeaderCountsCache() first so those counts still refresh correctly instead of reading stale (pre-population) cached values.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: PERFORMANCE.org Step 2 (extend Fix C to Sort, single-table mode): applyMultiSortColumnTints() now skips filter-hidden rows when computing shade-toggle boundaries, so tint bands reflect only the visible rows again — after WIP.1 the tbody permanently holds the full row set (hidden rows kept as display:none instead of removed), which previously let hidden rows shift the tint boundaries. The CAA/EAA big-picture strip's image order no longer freezes at its original fetch-time order after a sort: WIP.1 stopped calling initCaaPics()/initEaaPics() on every action, which used to rebuild the strip (and incidentally re-sort it) on every filter/sort pass; a new _artReorderBigBoxForTable() (plus caaReorderBigBoxForTable()/eaaReorderBigBoxForTable() wrappers) now cheaply moves the existing wrapper elements to match the table's new row order via box.appendChild — no rebuild, called once per sort from the sort handler right after it reorders the live tbody rows. The single-table sort path's own live-DOM-reorder (rows moved to match the new sort order before runFilter()'s show/hide pass runs, including the cdtoc tracklist sub-row fix) had already landed as part of WIP.1.

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: runFilter()'s in-place single-table filter path (PERFORMANCE.org Step 1) never re-synced a collapsed multi-row cell's mb-collapse-toggle-has-match indicator after applying a NEW filter's highlight, because initCollapsableColumns() — the only place that used to stamp that class — now runs once at initial render instead of after every filter pass. A match landing inside an already-built, already-collapsed cell (e.g. selecting a 'Join phrases' value like 'Featuring' that only matches a hidden <li>) showed no red/yellow 'hidden match' cue until the user manually expanded and re-collapsed that specific cell, which recomputes has-match via a separate, correct code path (ensureCollapseDelegate's click handler). Fixed by calling the existing _syncCollapseHasMatchInTable() helper (already used by applySubFilter() for the identical sub-table-filter case) right after the in-place show/hide pass, alongside the CAA/EAA bigbox sync that already runs there for the same 'used to happen via the old per-pass rebuild, now needs an explicit call' reason. The multi-table path (renderGroupedTable(), which still calls initCollapsableColumns() per sub-table on every filter pass) was unaffected.

sections.label: 🔧 Refactor
items: PERFORMANCE.org Step 1 (filter re-render, single-table mode): runFilter() no longer clones matching rows, replaces the tbody, or re-runs the post-render hook chain (initCollapsableColumns and the CAA/EAA/ERG/CDtoc it drives, plus Picard rewiring) on every keystroke. allRows are now kept as the live DOM rows throughout the session; each filter pass strips stale highlight spans and applies display:none / display:'' directly on those rows, then syncs the CAA/EAA bigbox via the existing caaUpdateBigBoxForTable()/eaaUpdateBigBoxForTable() helpers (previously only used by sub-table filters). The hook chain now runs exactly once — already true for the live fetch pipeline (startFetchingProcess), and newly hoisted into the disk-load/hydration path (initCollapsableColumns moved after updateH2Count() so its global toggle button can find filterContainer already attached; initCaaPics/initEaaPics/initCaaInlinePics/initEaaInlinePics called directly there since runFilter() no longer initialises them for single-table mode). Sort reorders the live tbody rows in place (appendChild loop) before the show/hide filter pass runs, so visible rows stay in sorted order. Fixed a regression the show/hide approach would otherwise introduce for cdtoc pages: a filtered-out or re-sorted row's tracklist sub-row (a synthetic sibling <tr> from _cdtocInitTracklistToggles(), not part of allRows) is now hidden/moved alongside its parent row instead of being orphaned.
